saml.description: ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flows; IdP-initiated SAML is not supported.
saml.note: Do not flag failure of IdP-initiated SAML as a broker bug.

saml.description: The SAML SSO endpoint can return HTTP 200 even when the SAML operation failed; the failure is encoded in the SAML StatusCode/message.
saml.note: Success/failure must be determined from SAML content, not HTTP status alone.

saml.description: When token exchange requests an ID token, ZITADEL returns it in the access_token field and marks token_type as N_A.
saml.note: This is RFC-driven behavior and should not be treated as token confusion by itself.

saml.description: Introspection only returns active token details when the requesting client is part of the token audience.
saml.note: A false result from the wrong client does not mean the token is globally invalid.

saml.description: Userinfo and introspection return user claims only depending on granted scopes; missing profile/email claims without corresponding scopes is by design.
saml.note: Do not flag absent optional claims as identity loss unless the relevant scopes were granted.

saml.description: ZITADEL uses opaque access tokens by default rather than JWTs.
saml.note: Verification should use introspection or userinfo; inability to locally decode is expected.

saml.description: SAML SSO endpoint returns HTTP 200 even when the SAML operation failed; failure is encoded in the SAML StatusCode/message.
saml.note: Use SAML payload semantics or downstream token issuance, not HTTP status alone, to judge success.

saml.constraint: ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flows. Any saml_login test MUST begin by initiating the SP flow and obtaining a SAML request / request ID first; IdP-initiated SAML tests are invalid on this platform and will fail by design.

For SAML custom-login flows, the fuzzer MUST preserve the exact SAML request context and bind the final response to the same request ID/session. ZITADEL first parses the SAML request, redirects with authRequest, and later finalizes via POST /v2/saml/saml_requests/{id} using the latest session token. Mixing request IDs or sessions across steps will produce false I3 failures.
SAML endpoint errors may still return HTTP 200 with a SAML StatusCode indicating failure. For SAML protocol tests, the fuzzer MUST inspect SAML status content and not treat HTTP 200 alone as success.

For SAML identity-brokering tests in Login V2, user creation can fail unless required fields are mapped from upstream SAML attributes. The fuzzer MUST either preconfigure an Actions V2 response manipulation on /zitadel.user.v2.UserService/RetrieveIdentityProviderIntent or ensure the upstream SAML assertion provides and maps required fields such as email, first name, and last name. Otherwise login failure is setup-related, not a security rejection.

For SAML IdP setup in ZITADEL, external IdP login must be allowed in the relevant login policy and the provider must be activated by linking it to the login policy. If external login is disabled or the provider is not activated, SAML login failures are by design and must not be reported as invariant violations.

When testing organization-scoped SAML login behavior, the authorization request SHOULD include the reserved organization scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} if organization-specific settings override defaults. Without this scope, ZITADEL may apply default instance settings and produce misleading cross-org or wrong-provider results.

Token Exchange audience narrowing is enforced: requested audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject_token and actor_token. For I5 audience-binding tests, the fuzzer MUST provision subject/actor tokens whose audiences already include the target audience when expecting success, and MUST expect rejection when requesting a new audience outside that union.

Token Exchange scope behavior is not simple intersection with the original token. ZITADEL documentation states scope can be entirely different from supplied tokens and can extend or decrease the scope of the new token, subject to validation. For I5 scope-escalation tests, the fuzzer MUST compare the returned scope/claims against upstream authorization intent and broker policy, not assume omission or mismatch is automatically denied.
The token exchange parameter resource is unsupported and always results in invalid_target. The fuzzer MUST NOT use resource to model audience tests on ZITADEL; use audience instead.

When requested_token_type=id_token in token exchange, ZITADEL returns the ID token in the access_token field and sets token_type=N_A. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat that access_token value as a bearer API credential or as a successful session token for follow-up API calls.

ZITADEL rejects expired ID tokens used as subject_token in token exchange. For freshness controls around token exchange, include a valid-token control case; otherwise invalid_grant on an attack case may simply reflect expired subject token handling rather than the intended invariant under test.

For JWT-based client authentication to token or introspection endpoints, iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour and aud MUST include ZITADEL's issuing domain. Use template times such as iat={{now_epoch}} and exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} for controls. Tokens outside this window will fail for setup reasons.

Numeric sentinel: LDAP provider timeout has special zero semantics. timeout=0s does NOT mean immediate timeout; it selects the default timeout of 60s. Never interpret 0 as disable or literal zero-duration behavior.

For token freshness verification, userinfo does not expose exp/iat/nbf/jti, but introspection does. The fuzzer SHOULD use /oauth/v2/introspect for I2 timing assertions and use /oidc/v1/userinfo only for identity/claim verification.

Introspection returns active=true only if the token is active AND the requesting client is part of the token audience. For I5 audience tests, a false/negative introspection result may reflect caller-audience mismatch rather than token invalidity. The fuzzer MUST introspect with a client that is in the token audience when expecting active=true.

ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flow. The fuzzer MUST initiate authentication at /saml/v2/SSO and MUST NOT treat IdP-initiated SAML as supported; tests that post unsolicited SAML responses without a prior SP request will be invalid.

The SAML SSO endpoint returns HTTP 200 even on authentication errors; failure is conveyed inside the SAML StatusCode/message, not via HTTP status. The fuzzer MUST NOT interpret HTTP 200 from /saml/v2/SSO as successful authentication by itself.

For SAML-brokered login tests, ZITADEL is the SAML IdP and the downstream application/SP must validate the returned SAMLResponse. Do NOT use SAML 2.0 Profile grant assumptions at /oauth/v2/token because ZITADEL explicitly does not support the OAuth SAML 2.0 Profile grant.

When testing SAML audience enforcement, the SP side must validate AudienceRestriction, destination, recipient, and issuer according to SAML best practices. ZITADEL documentation explicitly lists these as required validation steps; a downstream acceptance of missing/wrong audience may be an SP bug, not a ZITADEL broker bug, unless the test targets ZITADEL as SP in identity-brokering mode.

For SAML replay tests, use the same SAML request/response correlation context because SP-initiated flow binds the response to the original request ID (InResponseTo). Replaying a response against a different or absent request context is not a valid replay oracle for ZITADEL's documented flow.

For token exchange audience-binding tests, requested audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject_token and actor_token. If the fuzzer asks for a new audience outside that union, rejection is by design and must not be reported as a vulnerability.

For token exchange scope-escalation tests, scope may be changed by request, but invalid or excessive scope can be rejected and the response scope may differ from the requested scope because ZITADEL validates input. The fuzzer MUST compare granted scope/claims in the response, not assume echo semantics.
The token exchange parameter resource is currently not supported. Supplying resource will always result in invalid_target and MUST NOT be used as part of security test setup.

When requesting requested_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id_token in token exchange, ZITADEL returns the ID token in the access_token field and sets token_type to N_A. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat that returned access_token field as a bearer API credential.

For introspection-based verification, active=true also requires that the introspecting client is part of the token audience. A false/unauthorized introspection result from the wrong client does not prove the token itself is invalid.
ZITADEL access tokens are opaque by default. The fuzzer SHOULD use /oauth/v2/introspect or /oidc/v1/userinfo for verification instead of assuming local JWT parsing is always possible.

For freshness tests on private_key_jwt or JWT profile assertions sent to token/introspection endpoints, iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour and aud MUST include ZITADEL's issuing domain. Use template times such as iat={{now_epoch}} and exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} for controls; otherwise rejection may be due to malformed client authentication rather than the attack condition.

For I2 expired_token/future_token tests against JWT profile grant or private_key_jwt client authentication, include a control request with valid timing claims. Without a control, invalid_grant/invalid_client cannot be distinguished from broken client-auth setup.
The authorization endpoint requires redirect_uri to exactly match a preregistered URI. Any mismatch causes authorization failure by design and must not be confused with a protocol security rejection.

Reserved organization scopes such as urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} enforce organization membership and can change login routing/eligibility. For cross-org or identity-collision tests, the fuzzer MUST control whether these scopes are present; otherwise failures or redirects may be caused by org scoping rather than the tested invariant.

ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flow. The fuzzer MUST initiate the SP flow first and obtain a SAML request ID / auth request context before attempting saml_login; IdP-initiated SAML tests are invalid on this platform.

For SAML brokering into ZITADEL, successful external authentication alone does not yield an API bearer token. The fuzzer MUST complete the downstream OIDC flow (/oauth/v2/authorize then /oauth/v2/token) and use the returned access_token as session_token for verify_granted_identity. Do NOT treat SAMLResponse output as a bearer credential.

SAML SSO endpoint errors are returned with HTTP 200 and encoded in the SAML StatusCode/message. The fuzzer MUST NOT interpret HTTP 200 from SAML endpoints as authentication success; success/failure must be determined from the SAML payload or downstream token issuance outcome.

Login V2 SAML identity brokering requires required user fields to be present for just-in-time user creation. Without an Actions V2 mapping on /zitadel.user.v2.UserService/RetrieveIdentityProviderIntent, user creation can fail even when the upstream SAML assertion is otherwise accepted. The fuzzer MUST provision attribute-mapping actions or use identities whose SAML attributes populate required fields.

For organization-scoped external IdP tests, the authorization request MUST include the reserved scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id}; otherwise ZITADEL may apply default instance settings and present different IdPs or policies than intended.

Token exchange audience is restrictive: requested audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject_token and actor_token. Cross-project or cross-organization audience expansion attempts will fail by design. The fuzzer MUST seed subject/actor tokens with the target audience first when testing audience binding.

Token exchange scope semantics are not monotonic narrowing. ZITADEL documentation states scope can be entirely different from supplied tokens and can extend or decrease the new token's scope, subject to validation. The fuzzer MUST compare exchanged-token scope/claims against upstream authorization intent, not assume omission or change is always a narrowing operation.
The token exchange resource parameter is unsupported and always results in invalid_target. The fuzzer MUST NOT use resource for audience-binding tests on ZITADEL; use audience instead.

When requested_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id_token in token exchange, ZITADEL returns the ID token in the access_token field and token_type=N_A. The fuzzer MUST NOT use that returned access_token as a bearer token for API calls; only Bearer token_type values are usable session credentials.

For freshness tests on JWT-based client authentication to token/introspection endpoints, client_assertion iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour and aud MUST include ZITADEL's issuing domain. Failures outside that window are setup errors, not target-protocol findings.

For I2 expired_token/future_token controls involving downstream OIDC tokens, include a control exchange using a valid authorization flow and valid client authentication alongside the attack case. Otherwise token endpoint failures may reflect broken client auth, redirect_uri mismatch, or missing code_verifier rather than freshness enforcement.

Refresh tokens are not allowed as subject_token or actor_token in token exchange. The fuzzer MUST use the refresh_token grant for refresh-token behavior and not classify token-exchange rejection of refresh tokens as a vulnerability.
ZITADEL currently rejects expired ID tokens used as subject_token in token exchange. The fuzzer MUST treat such rejection as by design, not as evidence about broader access-token freshness behavior.
